cover: Five questions before you build a mobile app

slides.title: What does it need that a browser can't give?
slides.body: Daily camera or location use, working without a signal, notifications people rely on. If it's nothing, lean web.

slides.title: Do users need to work offline?
slides.body: Working in a warehouse or out in the field, with changes syncing later? That points to an installed app.

slides.title: Would people add you to the home screen?
slides.body: On iPhone, web push works only after they do. Most don't, so notifications people must see favor an app.

slides.title: Who maintains it a year from now?
slides.body: A team that writes JavaScript or TypeScript fits React Native. Flutter uses Dart and draws its own interface.

slides.title: Do customers expect you in an app store?
slides.body: Then build a real app. Apple's review guidelines say an app should do more than repackage a website.

slides.title: Reading your answers
slides.body: Nothing needed from the phone and no store expected: build web. Otherwise build cross-platform, native only where needed.
